name: Aliaxin

lead: Aliaxin is a range of hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers with different formulations designed for different facial tissues, from deeper volume and contour to softer fine-line work. Clinicians inject them to restore or add volume and to improve lines, folds and facial harmony.

Published work includes laboratory characterisation of the formulations, an animal biocompatibility study, small clinical series and a case series of combination protocols. The papers describe the gels' properties and results in small groups of patients.

paras: Treatment is performed in a clinic: a practitioner selects a formulation matched to the area (for example a more structural gel for shape and a softer one for overall softening) and injects it. Some protocols combine two Aliaxin products or follow with a skin-booster product. Results are visible soon after and last as long as the filler persists.

As with other HA fillers, bruising, swelling and lumps are expected side effects, and rare serious vascular complications are known across the category. HA fillers can be broken down with an enzyme, which a 2022 study examined for several products. Treatment should be given by a trained medical professional.

angle.text: The gel is placed where volume or contour is wanted, so the effect on the face is visible right after treatment. Different formulations are designed for deeper structure or softer, superficial work.

lead: Aliaxin is a line of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers from Italy, listed in the literature with several formulations such as Global Performance (AGP) and Shape and Restore (ASR).[1][2] Clinicians inject them into facial soft tissue to restore volume, support, and contour and to smooth lines.[2]

A 2016 characterisation paper tested the line's soluble-HA content, water uptake, rheology, resistance to enzymatic degradation and capacity to stimulate extracellular-matrix production, with the aim of matching each formulation to clinical indications.[1] Different formulations are described as targeting different soft-tissue layers, which affects recommended injection technique and result.[2]
Small clinical reports include a 2024 case series of four patients aged 35 to 55 who received ASR, AGP, or both, with the authors reporting support, lift, volume and softening.[2]
infobox: Global Performance (AGP), Shape and Restore (ASR), others
HA fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase

paras: The Aliaxin range is described in the scientific literature as a line of HA fillers with different physical properties for different facial indications.[1] The 2024 case series describes AGP and ASR as soft, highly cohesive gels that can be used alone or together for lift, volume and facial softening.[2]

Reported uses include nasolabial folds, facial rejuvenation and volume restoration. A clinical report found that injecting Aliaxin Global Performance followed by the skin-booster Viscoderm Skinko E gave larger improvements in nasolabial-fold hydration, transepidermal water loss and wrinkle appearance than Aliaxin Global Performance alone.[3]

A 2022 animal and laboratory study compared four HA products, including Aliaxin GP at 25 mg/mL cross-linked HA. Implants of cross-linked HA 25 mg/mL stayed visible on ultrasound for at least 33 weeks, compared with 4 weeks for a linear 8 mg/mL product, and enzyme-degradation tests were used to assess reversibility.[4]

In a guinea pig study, Aliaxin Global Performance and Viscoderm Skinko E did not cause significant inflammatory reactions and increased collagen and elastic fibres in the skin.[3] As with HA fillers generally, clinicians treat injection as a medical procedure.

Studies are small. A 2024 case series of four patients tested two formulations alone and in combination;[2] a 2016 paper combined an animal study with a clinical series in patients with moderate-to-severe nasolabial folds;[3] and a 2016 laboratory paper characterised the formulations.[1] No large randomised trial of the line is listed.

timeline.event: Biophysical and biological characterisation of the Aliaxin line published.[1]
Animal and clinical study of Aliaxin Global Performance with Viscoderm Skinko E published.[3]
